recommendation_1: Reduce the hidden dimension in the fully connected layers from 128 to 32 to drastically decrease the number of trainable parameters and memory footprint.
rationale_1: The current architecture uses 128 hidden units which significantly increases parameter count and memory usage; reducing this to 32 will substantially lower both RAM requirements and computational overhead without sacrificing too much accuracy.
recommendation_3: Implement Bfloat16 Autocast during training and inference to reduce memory usage and accelerate computations on CPU platforms without compromising numerical stability.
rationale_3: Using bf16 precision decreases memory consumption and increases throughput on CPUs, aligning well with low-power deployment scenarios typical in federated learning environments.
recommendation_4: Apply L1 Unstructured Pruning to remove redundant weights from the fully connected layers, specifically targeting the fc1 and fc2 layers to further compress the model size.
rationale_4: Pruning removes unnecessary connections, decreasing model size and improving energy efficiency while keeping the state_dict clean for seamless integration with Flower's aggregation mechanisms.
recommendation_5: Replace ReLU activation with Swish (SiLU) activation function to enhance gradient flow and reduce the likelihood of dead neurons, contributing to better convergence and lower energy usage.
rationale_5: Swish activation functions have been shown to improve training dynamics and can lead to more efficient models, especially when combined with other optimization techniques like pruning and quantization.
recommendation_6: Remove dropout regularization since it introduces additional computational overhead and does not contribute meaningfully to energy efficiency or memory reduction in this context.
rationale_6: Dropout adds complexity to forward passes and increases memory usage due to temporary storage of random masks; removing it simplifies the architecture and improves overall efficiency.
